To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fried ground beef contains a highly purified fraction that inhibits mutagenesis in a bacterial test system, and the initiation of skin tumors in mice.
fried ground beef contains substances (designated as CLA) that inhibit the initiation of mouse skin cancer by 7, 12 dimethylbenzanthracene.
a fraction from fried ground beef inhibits mutagenesis in Salmonella and the initiation of mouse skin carcinogenesis by 7, 12 dimethylbenza [a]anthraeene (DMBA).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of anticarcinogens from cooked meat.
the identification of anticarcinogens in foods and the elucidation of their mechanism(s) of action.
the identification, characterization and quantitation of heat altered derivatives of polyunsaturated fatty acids in fried beef.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CLA isomers are anticarcinogens.
the CLA isomers are potent inhibitors of DMBA induced mouse skin carcinogenesis.
CLA inhibits the initiation of epidernal carcinogenesis in the mouse by DMBA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CLA inhibits the formation of tumors by inhibiting the initiation phase of carcinogenesis.
the CLA fraction isolated from fried ground beef inhibits cytochrome P450 activity in vitro, and inhibits the initiation of skin carcinogenesis by DMBA in mice.
CLA is an effective anti initiation agent for mouse skin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CLA isomers are potent inhibitors of initiation of epidermoid carcinogenesis in mice and that they are present in fried ground beef.
there are substances in fried ground beef that can inhibit the initiation of skin cancer by DMBA and inhibit cytochrome P-450 activity in vitro.
CLA is an anticarcinogen that inhibits initiation of skin tumors in mice by DMBA, and that CLA is present in the fraction isolated from fried ground beef.
